evidence.label: Response time
evidence.caption: How much slower we are answering this account. Slow replies make a supply problem feel like neglect.
evidence.definition: Median (first_response_at - opened_at), last 4 weeks vs baseline.

evidence.label: Nephrologist visit gap
evidence.caption: Doctors who stop being visited tend to prescribe less over time. This catches the gap early.
evidence.definition: Days since last rep visit to a nephrologist linked to a hospital/clinic account, vs that prescriber's usual cadence.

evidence.label: Touchpoints
evidence.caption: How much less we are in touch with this account. Relationships fade quietly before orders fall.
evidence.definition: Visits+calls+WhatsApp touchpoints per 4 weeks vs baseline.

narrative.text: Sentinel found 2 independent source systems moving together: Response time +92% vs this account's own normal; Nephrologist visit gap 52 days vs a usual 8 days; Touchpoints -83% vs this account's own normal.
Visit gap, rep coverage or touchpoint drop: Nephrologist visit gap 52 days vs a usual 8 days; Touchpoints -83% vs this account's own normal.
The cause rule that fits best is field coverage gap; the customer-side symptoms follow from it rather than from a demand change.
Organizational memory's closest match is INC-014 (Hospital pharmacy relationship lapsed during long rep absence), resolved by: Late reassignment of coverage after tender cycle opened.

steps.action: Confirm the vacancy and list accounts in the territory by value and visit gap
Assign named interim cover from a neighbouring territory
Introduce the interim rep to key account contacts
Schedule visits to accounts with the largest visit gaps first
Monitor interaction frequency and orders until the vacancy is filled
Request a meeting with pharmacy procurement
